text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1: latency SLO breach detected for /v1/stream/* on hosted-gpu-pool-us-west. p95 ~= 1.2s -> 2.8s, p99 ~= 2.0s -> 5.3s. Paging oncall @lee and SRE rotation.

lee (oncall): seeing alerts. thanks. pulling up dashboards now. any correlated deploys?

maria (sre): no deploys in the last 30m. tracing shows tail spikes on streaming shards 7-10. streaming stalls and long token generation stalls reported.

jonathan (infra): checking infra metrics — GPU util across pool is spiky, but not uniformly high. one host (gpu-uw2-42) shows sustained 98% memcpy and 90% enc. IO wait on that host is high.

support-ops: we have two customers reporting degraded streaming: AcmePayments (prod) and EduFlow (staging -> prod traffic). both experiencing token dropouts and timeouts at ~10-20s.

kate (pm): any immediate mitigation recommended? customers are noticing.

maria (sre): initial hypothesis: noisy-tenant in the shared pool causing kernel-level IO or PCIe bus contention, cascading into long serialization stalls in the runtime. p99 tokens correspond to time spent in nvlink memcpy + blocked on host IO.

jonathan (infra): grabbing top processes on gpu-uw2-42:
```
# ps aux --sort=-%mem | head
root      1221  0.3  1.1  234k  54m ?        Ssl  09:10   0:02 /usr/bin/python3 -m inference_worker --tenant=fast-batch --task=decode
redwood   2234 45.1  0.8 2.3g  41m ?        Sl   09:12   5:12 /opt/bin/llm-serving --model=gptj-6b --tenant=heavy-renders
```
Looks like a heavy-renders job pegging memory copy and GPU kernels.

lee (oncall): can we isolate/migrate that tenant off the shared pool?

maria (sre): yes. run `redwoodctl routing migrate --tenant heavy-renders --destination dedicated-gpu-pool-temp --mode drain` to move new requests and drain existing ones. recommending immediate small-scale migration to reduce contention.

jonathan (infra): starting migration now. also raising blkio weight on that cgroup as temporary measure: `echo 500 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/llm-tenant-heavy-renders/blkio.weight` (current 100).

incident-bot: migration started (run id: run-1776008500-1). estimated drain ~3-7 minutes.

maria (sre): watch p99. if not improved in 5m, we'll evict long-running decode tasks and restart runtime on that host.

support-ops: informing AcmePayments that we're investigating; ETA 10m for mitigation.

jonathan (infra): snapshot of `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` shows high SM utilization + sustained memcopy. also `iostat -x 1 3` shows high await on nvme0n1: 300-600ms. possible host-level IO storm from sidecar logs or model cache misses.

maria (sre): can someone check if model cache was being populated (large downloads)? `du -sh /var/cache/model-cache/*`

jonathan (infra): model-cache shows a 12GB cold model fetch for `heavy-renders:v2` around 09:05. cache thrash combined with concurrent writes could explain blkio spike.

lee (oncall): migration progress?

incident-bot: migration run-1776008500-1: 60% moved, 10 active sessions draining, avg drain time 40s.

maria (sre): p95 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.4s after migration kick-off, p99 trending down but still at ~2.6s. good signal.

support-ops: AcmePayments confirmed partial improvement but still seeing occasional stalls.

jonathan (infra): I initiated a targeted eviction of 3 stuck `decode` workers on gpu-uw2-42 (`kill -9 PID`) and restarted the runtime process for that host: `systemctl restart redwood-runtime`.

maria (sre): after restart, p99 for stream endpoint is 1.1s. no more streaming stalls from that host. marking host as reprovision candidate for deeper tracing.

customer-impact-bot: Notifying customers: AcmePayments (incident advisory), EduFlow (info). Support ticket #INC-3124 created.

lee (oncall): assigning incident P1 -> mitigation in progress. Please add all actions to the incident runbook.

kate (pm): timeline for customers — when can we confirm fully resolved? they want postmortem and whether they need to shift to Dedicated.

maria (sre): short term: migration + eviction + blkio bump + runtime restart fixed it. Root cause probable: large model cache population by heavy-renders tenant combined with sustained kernel memcpy usage (noisy tenant) causing host IO and GPU memcpy stalls.

jonathan (infra): next steps: quarantine offending tenant from shared pools, add prefetch throttling for model-cache (rate limit downloads), and add cgroup blkio auto-adjust heuristics to limit any single tenant's IO weight to 200 by default.

support-ops: logged impacted customers + SLA hit calc. AcmePayments had ~2.3% request error/timeout spike during 09:05-09:20 window.

maria (sre): long-term: consider route-based isolation flags so customers running large batch inference land in Dedicated or in per-tenant cached nodes. Also add streaming stall synthetic checks to catch token-level stalls earlier.

lee (oncall): handing off to next oncall @maria in 20m. summary for handoff: P1 latency SLO breach due to noisy tenant heavy-renders; mitigation applied: migrate tenant, blkio weight bump, evicted stuck workers, restarted runtime on gpu-uw2-42. Current status: p95/p99 back within SLO, monitoring for 30m. next actions: quarantine tenant, implement cache prefetch throttle, postmortem + customer comms.

maria (sre): acknowledged. I'll keep watch and start the postmortem doc. tagging infra for follow-up items.

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated (monitoring). Please update the incident channel when resolved. :white_check_mark:
